title: The floating dirt, checked -- it was real and it is gone
question: Does the spoil read as a heap of dug-out dirt in front of the face now, or is there still something wrong with it?
context_md:
You were right, and it was worse than a blemish. Counted properly -- pieces of ground with **no path down to the floor**, not just cells with a gap under them -- the old build had 2 to 6 such pieces and mine had **26 to 38**. Ten times, and mine.

**Why it happened.** Spoil an ant puts down is cemented, the way it cements a tunnel wall, and cemented ground is the one thing in this world that does not fall -- that is the whole reason a tunnel stands. So anything that later dug out from under a pellet stranded it there permanently.

**Three things fixed it.** An ant now only puts a pellet somewhere it could actually lie: something solid under it, not balanced on a single cell, and open sky over it. Cemented ground that ends up touching almost nothing goes back to being loose dirt and falls -- grains pressed together need something to be pressed *against*. And when there is nowhere beside it that will do, the ant carries the pellet out of the burrow.

**And I owe you a correction.** Finding this showed that the nest sizes I quoted you were too generous, on *both* sides. The counter asks "is there ground somewhere above this hole" -- and a few crumbs hanging in the sky were answering yes for everything underneath them. With them gone, today's build measures 110 and 83 where I told you 197 and 179, and my build measures 17 and 20 where I told you 54 and 58. So the honest gap is bigger than I said, and it is worst in the lab's flat bed: an ant digging straight down keeps coming back up to put something down, so it drives shallower workings. On a bank it is much closer -- 69/95/62/66 against 132/115/100/134 over four seeds.

Still exact on the thing you asked for: nothing leaves the world.

items.label: A -- what you saw
items.caption: spoil stranded wherever it was left

items.label: B -- now
items.caption: same bank, same seed, same 8,000 frames
